evidence.note: Repeated deliberate test-counting across crates and app/tests, establishing awareness of the ~1,390-test horizon (the denominator for progress) before implementing.
Loads and creates a TodoWrite ledger to track remaining crate work — a lightweight progress-tracking mechanism.
Builds and tests the common crate, then updates the TodoWrite ledger after that result; the only observed instance of updating progress against verified test outcomes.

reasoning: The agent shows genuine early horizon-sizing (counting tests to know the total) and sets up a todo ledger that it updates once after completing the first leaf crate, placing it around the 'rough per-crate tracking' region (anchor 4-5). It does not exhibit the maintained per-binary pass-count ledger, regression-watching, or loop-detection of anchors 8-10 — and the trajectory ends after just the common crate, so sustained full-horizon accounting is simply not observable. I settle on 4 because what is present is real but minimal and unsustained.
